_comment: Storyboard for the Grade 3 Computing unit lecture film, Lesson 13 Systems, Inputs and Files. Rendered by tools/create-ehel-unit-lecture.js. See lecture-video/BRIEF.md. Chapters follow LESSON[lecture] in order (system; roles; inputs; files), then the recap. The lesson's docstring LESSON['lecture'] carries two more parts appended after the first four ('Automatic inputs that read you': biometric, RFID, a bus pass; 'Hardware and software, working as one system': an e-reader) - both are taught as extra beats on the END of the 'system' and 'inputs' chapters below, not as two new chapters, so the four-chapter shape and its four objective codes stay exactly as the lesson's own lecture order has them. THERE IS NO ART.sim for this lesson's ideas - a working system, hardware vs software roles, manual vs automatic input, file types - so every picture here is drawn in the engine's own idiom. The one kit piece borrowed is ART.figure('laptop'), which already carries a keyboard part and a screen part with their own tap outlines, so the K-press demo rings the lesson's own laptop rather than a laptop drawn from scratch.
title: Systems, Inputs and Files
subtitle: Grade 3 Computing
objectives: Know that the hardware and software components of computing devices combine to form a working system.
Know the differences between hardware and software, and compare the different roles that they perform in computer systems.
Identify a range of manual and automatic input devices.
Know that different types of file can be stored on a computer's hard drive, including text, audio, image, video and games.

beats.say: You press K on the keyboard, and a letter appears on the screen.
Hardware, software, hardware: one working system, made of parts with different jobs.
A keyboard with no software is just a box of buttons.
A program with no hardware has nowhere to run.
Press K, and the keyboard, hardware, sends a signal down the wire.

at.signal: sends a signal down the wire

beats.say: The operating system and the app, software, decide what it means.
The screen, hardware, shows the K. Hardware and software combine into one system.
An e-reader is a system too: hardware, plus software that shows the page.
No software: a screen shows nothing. No screen: software has nowhere to go.
Hardware is the parts you can touch: it senses, shows, stores and sounds.

at.job1: it senses, shows, stores and sounds

beats.say: Showing a picture: the screen is hardware. Deciding which picture: that is software.
Software is the instructions: it decides, calculates and works out what to do.
Storing a file: the hard drive is hardware. The program that saves it: software.
A program that works out 37 plus 48 is software, running on the processor.
Every job the computer does has a hardware half and a software half.

at.both: a hardware half and a software half

beats.say: An input can be manual: a person does it themself.
A keyboard, a mouse, a touchscreen, a microphone you speak into: all manual.
An input can be automatic: a sensor does it by itself, with no person.

at.sensor: a sensor does it by itself

beats.say: A thermometer, a light sensor, a barcode scanner: each senses without being asked.
The sensor on an automatic door spots you and opens it, all by itself.

at.door: The sensor on an automatic door

beats.say: Automatic does not mean better; it just means no person. Each kind is right for its job.
Automatic inputs read you: a fingerprint or a face. That is biometric.
Others read a tag: RFID. You wave it, like a bus pass, to get on.
The hard drive keeps files, and every file has a type.
A text file holds words, like a story. An audio file holds sound, like a song.
An image file holds a picture. A video file holds moving pictures with sound.

at.image: An image file holds a picture
at.video: A video file holds moving pictures with sound

beats.say: A game file holds a whole game, ready to run.

at.game: A game file holds a whole game

beats.say: Record yourself singing, and the file that is saved is audio: it holds sound.

at.audiofile: the file that is saved is audio

beats.say: The type decides what the file holds, and which program can open it.

at.decides2: The type decides what the file holds

beats.say: Hardware and software combine into one working system.
Hardware senses, shows and stores. Software decides and calculates.
Manual inputs need a person. Automatic inputs sense by themselves.
Text, audio, image, video, games: five types of file, on the hard drive.
